extracted.intended_audience: publicists / PR people and communicators who pitch journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and a practical rubric from a working journalist about what makes them delete, keep reading, or pursue a press release/pitch — including subject lines, openings, structure, embargoes, follow-ups, and spokesperson availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inbox triage metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line decides 90% of the time; If I open: first 2 lines decide; If I read past 2 lines: maybe a 30-second skim; Less than 5% reach a 'save for later' folder; Less than 0.5% become a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets expectations for conversion and attention span: pitches must win at subject line and the first two lines to survive a very short evaluation window (open → 2 lines → 30-second skim).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line — be specific and accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line specific and accurate; subject line that names a real number or named entity keeps me reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete facts (a number, a named entity) to signal newsworthiness. Accuracy is essential; misleading subject lines reduce trust and will get deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: What gets deleted immediately includes: Subject line in ALL CAPS; Subject line with 'EXCLUSIVE' when it's not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sensational formatting and false exclusivity. These come across as spam or dishonest and trigger instant deletion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening lines / first sentence must hook
rubrics_metrics.description: If I open: first 2 lines decide; First sentence that mentions my recent article; First sentence is the hook, not throat-clearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the very first sentence do the heavy lifting: reference the reporter's work when possible, present the angle/hook immediately, and avoid generic lead-ins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email body length and scannability
rubrics_metrics.description: More than 2 paragraphs in the email body leads to deletion; Short, scannable email body is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the body brief and easy to skim: use short paragraphs, bullets or clear line breaks so a 30-second skim communicates the news and the angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid cold template openings and clichés
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete triggers include 'I'm reaching out because...' (cold spam template) and 'Hope you're doing well in these unprecedented times'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't use generic, boilerplate intros that signal mass emailing; personalization and originality matter. Clichés waste the limited attention window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments must be contextualized (don't attach blindly)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment without any context in body and lines like 'Please find attached our press release' cause deletion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you include attachments, explain what they are and why they matter in the email body. Don't rely on an unexplained attachment to sell the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization to beat / reporter
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized to my beat; First sentence that mentions my recent article is effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show you've done your homework: name the reporter's beat or recent relevant coverage to demonstrate fit and increase the chance the pitch is read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer a specific story angle, not just an announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific story angle, not just the announcement, keeps me reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame the news as a story with an angle that matters to the publication's audience; don't simply forward an announcement without suggesting why it is newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about what you can offer
rubrics_metrics.description: Line 3 of the suggested pitch: 'What I can offer (interview, data, exclusive)'; 'If interested, I can have her on a call within 30 minutes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clearly whether you can provide interviews, data, exclusives, spokespeople and how quickly they can be available — immediacy and concreteness increase pickup likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson name, credentials, and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Spokesperson name + credentials in line 2; Spokesperson concrete and available; Sign-off with phone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put the spokesperson's name and why they matter early. Provide quick availability windows and direct contact details (phone number) so the journalist can act immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch structure that works (4-line template)
rubrics_metrics.description: Line 1: The hook (one sentence); Line 2: Why this matters / why now; Line 3: What I can offer (interview, data, exclusive); Line 4: Quick credentials / why this source matters; Sign-off with phone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this compact, ordered structure to maximize clarity in a tiny space. It maps to how journalists triage: hook → context → offer → credibility → contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't offer embargoes unless I cover the beat seriously; 24-48 hours is the sweet spot; Anything longer feels like manipulation; Breaking embargo is a career-ender for the source company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only propose embargoes to appropriate reporters; prefer short embargo windows (1–2 days); respect embargoes strictly — violating them damages relationships and reputations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: One follow-up max, after 3 business days; Don't ask if I 'saw your previous email'; Send a NEW angle in the follow-up; After 2 emails total: assume no, move on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit persistence and make follow-ups valuable: wait a few business days, add fresh information or a different hook, and stop after a single meaningful follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (explicit checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line specific and accurate; First sentence is the hook, not throat-clearing; Personalized to my beat; Spokesperson concrete and available; Story angle, not just announcement; Short, scannable email body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compact checklist summarizes the author's evaluative criteria and can be used as a pre-send checklist to self-audit pitches and press-release emails.
